summary: AnonAddy is a self-hosted email forwarding service designed to help you create and manage distinct aliases. By routing messages through a central server, it lets you hide your primary email address from third-party services. It is provided under the MIT licence and developed using PHP and Docker.
goodFor: It is a suitable choice for privacy-conscious users who want to host their own email routing infrastructure rather than relying on a managed third-party service.
watchOut: Operating your own email forwarding infrastructure carries a significant maintenance burden regarding domain reputation, DNS configuration, and reliable delivery to external inboxes.
deployNotes: As a PHP and Docker application, deployment typically involves setting up a container runtime, a persistent database backend, and a reverse proxy to handle TLS termination and incoming mail routing.
